page_0.title: Automation Exercise
page_0.summary:
- Purpose: E‑commerce demo/catalog page for browsing products, viewing product details, adding items to a shopping cart, and accessing account, help and API/testing resources.
- Main flows: navigate categories (WOMEN/MEN/KIDS and subcategories), open product detail (View Product), add items to cart (Add to cart → View Cart), signup/login and proceed to checkout; access Test Cases/API Testing/Video Tutorials/Contact Us pages.
- Other actions: filter by brand (brand names with product counts), view cart summary, navigate site header links.
- Key UI elements to test: header navigation links, category and brand filters, product cards, View Product modal/page, Add to cart button behavior, View Cart page, Signup/Login forms, Contact/Help pages, API list page.
- Edge case — cart behavior: adding same item multiple times, quantity updates, cart persistence across refresh or login/logout, removing items, empty cart handling.
- Edge case — data consistency: brand count vs actual items shown, price/total calculation, promotions or zero/negative quantities, out-of-stock or deleted products.
- Edge case — auth flows: guest checkout vs logged-in, session expiry during checkout, invalid/duplicate signup, forgotten-password flows.
- Edge case — resilience: slow/failing API responses, broken links/icons (e.g., special icon text " Products"), missing images, malformed product data.
- Edge case — UI/UX: responsiveness on mobile, truncated labels, pagination/large result handling, keyboard accessibility and ARIA/assistive tech support.

page_1.title: Automation Exercise - All Products
page_1.summary:
- Purpose: product listing/catalog page to browse all products, filter by category/brand, view product details, and add items to the shopping cart.
- Primary flows: navigate site (Home, Products, Contact us, Test Cases, Video Tutorials, API Testing), filter by category (WOMEN/MEN/KIDS), filter by brand, click View Product for details, click Add to cart and View Cart, use Signup / Login for account-required actions, use #scrollUp to return to top.
- Key UI interactions: product tiles with Add to cart and View Product buttons, category/brand links with item counts, site-wide header navigation links.
- Important edge cases — functional: Add to cart when item has variants/quantity not selected, Add to cart from listing vs product page (consistency), attempting cart actions when not logged in, empty filter results, pagination/infinite-scroll load failures.
- Important edge cases — data/state: out-of-stock or inventory mismatch after adding, cart/session persistence across refresh/login/logout, duplicate rapid-clicks adding multiples, price/discount mismatch between listing and detail.
- Important edge cases — environmental/accessibility: JS disabled or slow network causing broken Add/View actions, broken links for header items, responsive layout hiding buttons on small screens, #scrollUp anchor behavior on long pages.

page_2.title: Automation Exercise - Checkout
page_2.summary:
- Main purpose: display the user's shopping cart and enable progression toward checkout (view/remove/update cart items) while providing site navigation and an email subscription entry point.  
- Primary user flows: navigate via header links (Home, Products, Cart, Signup/Login, Test Cases, API Testing, Video Tutorials, Contact us); view cart contents and proceed to checkout; sign up / log in; submit an email to subscribe (#susbscribe_email + #subscribe); use #scrollUp to jump to top.  
- Important edge cases to test: empty cart state and transitions after adding/removing items; invalid or blank subscription email and client/server validation; mismatched/typo ID (#susbscribe_email) or missing label affecting automation selectors; broken or redirecting header links (including ambiguous "here"); session/cart persistence across login/logout and page reloads; concurrent updates (quantity changed in another tab); slow network / timeouts and UI feedback; keyboard accessibility and focus behavior for #scrollUp and subscribe.

page_3.title: Automation Exercise - Signup / Login
page_3.summary:
- Main purpose: allow users to create accounts, sign in, and subscribe to newsletters; acts as the authentication entry point and gateway to shopping pages.
- Main user flows: Signup (create account), Login (authenticate), Newsletter subscribe, navigation to Home/Products/Cart/Test Cases/API Tutorials/Contact pages, and page scroll-up.
- Key interactive controls: Login and Signup buttons, subscribe button, multiple form inputs including #susbscribe_email.
- Input/validation flows to test: empty fields, invalid email formats, password length/complexity, leading/trailing whitespace, max-length and very-long inputs, duplicate-email signup.
- Authentication edge cases: incorrect credentials, case-sensitivity, account lockout/rate-limiting, password reset absent/visible, session persistence and logout behavior.
- Security and injection checks: SQL injection/XSS in form fields, CSRF on forms, behavior under rapid repeated requests.
- UI/UX and robustness: responsiveness across viewports, keyboard/tab order and focus, error message clarity, button disabled/enabled states, network error handling and form state after navigation.

page_4.title: Automation Practice for API Testing
page_4.summary:
- Main purpose: a catalog page listing available API endpoints for the Automation Exercise site so testers can discover and exercise endpoints (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE) such as products, brands, search, login, register, and user account operations.
- Main user flows: navigate site menu (Home, Products, Cart, Signup/Login, Test Cases, API Testing, Contact); select an API entry to view/use that endpoint; perform API actions (GET product list, POST search/login/register, PUT/DELETE for update/remove); sign up/login for endpoints that require authentication.
- Key endpoints to exercise explicitly: Get All Products, POST/PUT/DELETE on Brands, POST Search Product, POST Verify Login, POST Create/Register, DELETE/PUT user operations, GET user account details.
- Important edge cases — malformed/partial labels and truncated UI text (verify full names and links resolve correctly).
- Missing/duplicate URL labels (multiple items show the same base URL) — validate each endpoint target and parameterization is unique and correct.
- Authorization-required flows: test authenticated vs unauthenticated access, token expiry, invalid or missing credentials.
- Input validation: invalid JSON, missing required fields, excessive payload size, SQL/JS injection attempts, and boundary values for search/filter parameters.
- HTTP method edge cases: method not allowed responses when using wrong methods, unexpected status codes (500, 404), and inconsistent response schemas.
- Network/CORS and rate limiting: simulate slow/failed connections, CORS restrictions, and rate-limit behavior.

page_5.title: Automation Exercise - Product Details
page_5.summary:
- Main purpose: a product details page (product id 1) to show item info, let users add to cart, view cart, and submit a product review while providing site navigation and category/brand filters.
- Primary navigation flows: click Home/Products/Cart/Signup-Login/Test Cases/API/Video Tutorials/Contact Us and top/breadcrumb links to move between pages.
- Product/category flows: browse WOMEN/MEN/KIDS categories, filter by subcategories (Dress/Tops/etc.) and brands (POLO, H&M, etc.), then view product details and "Continue Shopping" or "View Cart".
- Cart flow: add product to cart from this page, view cart, and continue shopping or proceed to checkout.
- Review flow: open "WRITE YOUR REVIEW", enter rating/title/body, submit review (may require authentication).
- Utility flows: use #scrollUp and other UI controls (View Cart, Continue Shopping).
- Important edge cases: submitting empty/oversized/HTML/JS payloads in review (XSS/validation), submitting duplicate reviews, guest vs authenticated review restrictions.
- Cart edge cases: add zero/negative/very large quantity, concurrent updates (race conditions), session expiration or cart persistence across sessions.
- Navigation/availability edge cases: broken links, product not found/removed, slow network/timeouts, and mobile/responsive layout issues.

page_6.title: Automation Exercise - Polo Products
page_6.summary:
- Purpose: Brand-specific product listing page showing "Polo" products (URL: /brand_products/Polo) where users can browse items and add them to cart or view details.
- Main flows: navigate site header (Home, Products, Contact us, Test Cases, API Testing, Video Tutorials); filter/choose category (WOMEN/MEN/KIDS) and brand; click "View Product" to see details; "Add to cart" from listing; "View Cart" to proceed.
- Secondary flows: user authentication (Signup / Login) before checkout; navigation between product pages and categories; use header cart link.
- Key UI elements to exercise: product tiles, brand list with counts (e.g., POLO (6)), Add to cart buttons, View Product buttons, View Cart link.
- Edge case — mismatch: brand count number vs actual items displayed (counts incorrect or stale).
- Edge case — cart behavior: adding same item multiple times, quantity limits, cart persistence across navigation/refresh and logged-out vs logged-in sessions.
- Edge case — concurrency / rapid clicks: duplicate orders or multiple additions when Add to cart clicked repeatedly or offline/slow network.
- Edge case — item availability: adding out-of-stock items, items removed from catalog while in cart, or deleted product IDs.
- Edge case — navigation/broken links: header links (Test Cases, API Testing, Video Tutorials) or product View Product linking to wrong URL or 404.

page_7.title: Automation Practice Website for UI Testing - Test Cases
page_7.summary:
Purpose: a catalogue page that lists and links to the site’s predefined functional test cases (Test Case 1–20) for QA/reference.

Main user flows: navigate via top menu (Home, Products, Cart, Signup/Login, Test Cases), open individual test-case details, follow external/internal links (e.g., site root), and use flows referenced by test cases (register/login, search, add to cart, place order, contact form).

Concrete actions to validate: clicking each test-case opens the correct details; top-nav highlights/redirects work; truncated titles either expand or show full text/tooltip; links open in same or new tab as expected.

State-dependent flows to test: test-cases that require authentication (register/login, place order) should handle authenticated vs unauthenticated users and redirect or prompt appropriately.

Form-related flows: Contact Us, subscription, search and login forms need validation for valid/invalid/empty inputs, special characters, and large payloads.

Cart/order flows: adding/removing items, quantity updates, empty-cart behavior, checkout for registered vs guest users, concurrency (duplicate submissions).

Edge/negative cases: broken or 404 links, slow network/timeouts, session expiration, permission errors, duplicate submissions, DB/state cleanup between tests.

Accessibility/responsiveness: menu collapse/hamburger behavior on small screens, keyboard navigation, tooltip/aria for truncated titles, and cross-browser rendering.

page_8.title: Automation Exercise - Contact Us
page_8.summary:
- Purpose: a Contact Us page allowing users to send messages to site support and subscribe to a newsletter; also provides navigation to main site areas (Home, Products, Cart, Signup/Login, Test Cases, etc.).
- Main user flows: navigate via header links; submit the contact form (name/email/subject/message); click the feedback email link (mailto); enter email and click #subscribe to join newsletter; use #scrollUp to return to top.
- Primary elements to test: contact form inputs and textarea (#message), subscribe email input (#susbscribe_email) and button (#subscribe), header navigation links, mailto link, scroll-up control.
- Important validation cases: required-field enforcement, invalid-email formats, excessively long inputs, and whitespace-only inputs.
- Security/input-sanitization edge cases: script tags/HTML, SQL-like payloads, special/unicode characters, CRLF injection in subject or email.
- UX/error handling edge cases: missing or unclear success/error messages, form resubmission on refresh, submit button state during submission, timeout/network failure handling.
- Integration/link edge cases: broken/incorrect link targets, links opening in wrong window/tab, mailto behavior on devices without an email client.
- Rate/throttle edge cases: rapid repeated submissions, subscribe duplicates, and server-side rate limits or CAPTCHA triggers.

page_9.title: Automation Exercise - H&M Products
page_9.summary:
- Main purpose: display the H&M brand product listing so users can browse H&M items, view product details, and add items to the shopping cart on the Automation Exercise site.
- Main navigation flows: top navbar links (Home, Products, Cart, Signup / Login, Test Cases, API Testing, Video Tutorials, Contact us).
- Browsing flows: category navigation (WOMEN/MEN/KIDS → Dress, Tops, Tshirts, Jeans, etc.), brand filter selection (H&M, POLO, MADAME, etc.), product list interactions (View Product, Add to cart, View Cart).
- Checkout/login flow: add-to-cart → view cart → (presumably) proceed to checkout which may require Signup / Login.
- Product detail flow: clicking View Product opens product page with more details and purchase options.
- Important edge cases: Add to cart when product requires options (size/color) or is out of stock; adding same product multiple times (quantity aggregation vs duplicate line items).
- Important edge cases: incorrect or inconsistent brand counts (e.g., "(5) H&M" vs actual displayed items), broken or slow network causing partial renders of product list or failed add-to-cart.
- Important edge cases: navigation links/redirects broken (View Cart, View Product, or top navbar), session timeout or cookie issues losing cart contents, and unauthenticated actions blocked unexpectedly.
- Important edge cases: UI responsiveness/accessibility problems (buttons overlapped, modals not closing, mobile layout issues) and mismatch between UI feedback and actual cart state.
